name: Ireland: participant-facing document QC
source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/ireland/en/patient-facing-document-qc-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026), sections 1-9; population items also from the Ireland population guides' submission checks (named in each item); core SIS content from the Ireland patient information and consent guide (IE-ICF)
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

sections.title: Trial content (QC 3 and 4; IE-ICF core information)

items.check: Trial title, sponsor, phase, purpose and treatment allocation agree with the final protocol and other Part II forms.
The document explains in plain English that the activity is research and that participation is voluntary.
Why the person is invited and how many people will take part are stated.
What will happen, what is experimental and what differs from normal care are explained; research-specific procedures are distinguished from standard care.
The investigational treatment, comparator, placebo and the chance of receiving each arm are explained.
Reasonably foreseeable risks, burdens, discomforts, disadvantages and precautions are explained in understandable terms.
Expected benefits are stated, including a clear statement if there may be no personal benefit.
Relevant alternative treatment or care and the effect of declining are explained.
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, contraception and pregnancy-reporting requirements are explained.
Compensation, reimbursement, insurance, research-injury and complaint arrangements are explained.
What happens if the person stops, and what data and samples may lawfully remain, is explained.
Investigator, study-team, Data Protection Officer, rights, injury and complaint contacts are given.
New information that could affect willingness to continue will be provided, and this is stated.
The applicable cooling-off or reflection opportunity is given where practicable.
Where participants can find public trial information and results is stated.
Participants are not referred to the protocol, Investigator's Brochure or SmPC to discover material risks; the information needed for consent is in the document itself (IE-ICF).

sections.title: Protocol consistency (QC 3)
sections.instruction: Check every statement against the final protocol and the other Part II forms. Do not repair a protocol conflict only in the participant document: resolve the source discrepancy and update all affected files.

items.check: Visit number, visit length, study duration and follow-up period agree with the protocol.
Procedures, sample volumes, imaging, biopsies and optional substudies agree with the protocol.
Randomisation, placebo and blinding are described accurately.
Foreseeable risks, burdens, reproductive precautions and expected benefits agree with the protocol and IB or product information.
Rescue treatment, prohibited medicines and lifestyle restrictions agree.
Early withdrawal and sponsor termination consequences agree.
Pregnancy reporting and follow-up routes agree.

Treatment arms, doses, procedure counts, visit length, contraception, storage, retention, recipients, transfers, injury wording and contacts match the recruitment procedure, Irish data statement, compensation form and sample form (IE-ICF final review).
Each consent statement has a corresponding explanation in the information sheet.
Required trial participation is not mixed with optional choices; each optional activity is described before its consent statement.

Optional items have separate initials, tick boxes or signatures and can be declined independently; declining does not block main-study participation unless the activity is genuinely necessary, in which case it is explained and not presented as optional.
Consent to record access identifies the relevant monitors, auditors, regulators and authorised bodies.
Data and sample wording does not promise complete deletion where legal retention duties apply.
Signature blocks cover the participant or representative, the person conducting consent, and date and time where needed.
Guardian, legally designated representative, witness and interpreter blocks appear only in the versions that use them.
No pre-ticked boxes or bundled future-use permission appears.

sections.title: Population and consent-pathway coverage (QC 2; Ireland population guides)

items.check: Every population and inclusion pathway permitted by the protocol maps to a population with an appropriate information and consent route, populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage, and every population and optional procedure that changes the information or consent logic has the correct document; adults who can consent use the main SIS and ICF.

Healthy volunteers (IE-HV): information tailored to non-therapeutic participation; no therapeutic benefit claimed (screening, monitoring, payment or access to staff not described as benefit); unknown risk not minimised and prominent for first-in-human or novel-mechanism studies; prior human exposure, escalation, sentinel dosing and stopping rules explained; screening procedures, screening-failure handling and incidental findings covered; visits, confinement, sampling and restrictions complete; reproductive precautions match the protocol; payment itemised, separate from expenses and not contingent on completing every procedure; insurance and emergency contacts correct; repeat-volunteer checks explained; optional samples or future research have separate choices.

Participants aged 16-17 (IE-MINORS): own informed consent to participation and data processing; no parent or guardian consent required solely because of age; content matches the capable adult version in age-appropriate language.

Participants under 16 (IE-MINORS): parent or guardian consent document present with the full information, how the child will be informed and how dissent is handled; age-appropriate assent materials for each band the protocol needs, with the bands justified; the protocol age range matches every SIS, ICF and assent version; assent sought according to capacity, age and maturity; refusal and withdrawal respected; re-consent at 16 described; risks and burdens written for both guardian and child; school, family and social impacts addressed where relevant; young children not asked to sign adult legal or data-protection declarations; signature blocks match the actual pathway.

Adults unable to consent (IE-CAPACITY): accessible participant information plus full representative SIS and ICF; Irish legally designated representative hierarchy followed (personal relationship first, otherwise the treating medical practitioner not involved in the trial); Article 31 conditions addressed; the participant's will, preferences and dissent respected; trial participation consent separated from data-processing safeguards; representative signature block identifies the representative, relationship or role, person taking consent and date; re-consent after capacity returns is operational; no incentive for the incapacitated participant.

Emergency enrolment (IE-EMERGENCY): used only where the protocol and law allow deferred consent; all Article 35 conditions addressed, not selected individually; post-enrolment participant SIS and ICF explains why enrolment occurred before consent, what has already happened, current risks, alternatives and benefits, continued procedures, the right to refuse continued participation and what happens to data and samples already collected; representative documents and prompt participant re-consent present; the Irish data-processing safeguard is lawful and described.

Impartial witness (IE-WITNESS): included only where it may be needed; the participant or representative remains the decision-maker; fields for participant or representative name and mark or signature method, witness name, signature and date, witness confirmation of impartiality and attendance for the full discussion, the reason the witness was used, the person conducting consent, and interpreter details and attestation where a separate interpreter is used; translation and interpreting needs handled separately; the participant receives a copy of the completed consent record.

Pregnancy follow-up (IE-PREGNANCY): participant and partner pathways use separate documents; the pregnant partner consents for herself and the participant does not sign for her; data fields and follow-up duration match the protocol; medical-record and clinician access explicit and specifically permitted; maternal, fetal and infant data distinguished with a defined follow-up endpoint; optional collection separated from required safety reporting; withdrawal and legal retention accurate; contact methods protect confidentiality, with a choice of safe contact method; no language that pressures pregnancy decisions.
Optional future research (IE-SECONDARY): separated from trial participation (see section C6).
Optional genetics and other optional substudies (IE-PII-CHECKLIST item 3): a separate or clearly distinct version or consent section where the option changes the information or consent logic.

sections.title: Irish data-protection review (QC 6; IE-ICF data-protection information)
sections.instruction: Cross-check the participant documents against the NREC data-protection statement or DPIA (IE-R1), the sponsor privacy information and the protocol.

items.check: Controller and relevant contact details are consistent, including the Data Protection Officer.
Data categories, purposes, legal bases, recipients (Irish and international) and transfers with their safeguards agree.
Retention periods, or the method for setting them, agree and are realistic, with the legal or scientific reason; no open-ended 'as long as necessary' wording without explanation.
The documents distinguish consent to trial participation from the legal basis for processing personal data.
Any reliance on explicit consent as a Health Research Regulations safeguard is described accurately.
A legally designated representative is not asked to give explicit consent to data processing for an adult who lacks capacity.
Any required Health Research Consent Declaration Committee route is identified before submission and described consistently.
Pseudonymised or coded data are not described as anonymous.
Rights are explained accurately: withdrawal from future activities is possible, legal duties may require retention of data already collected, and the practical result and legal basis are stated.

sections.title: Biological samples and secondary use (QC 7; IE-SECONDARY)

items.check: Sample type, amount, collection method and immediate trial use are clear.
Storage location, duration, access, coding, transfer and destruction arrangements are clear; return of results and incidental findings and any commercial use are stated.
Genetic or genomic analysis is stated expressly where relevant.
Optional secondary use is separate from required protocol testing; declining does not affect trial participation or care.
Broad consent is limited to a described disease, health or research area; it is not permission for unspecified research.
Commercial access, international transfer, storage duration, governance and access controls, recontact and return-of-results policies are explicit.
Withdrawal consequences explain what can and cannot be retrieved or destroyed, without promising removal from backups, safety files or records that must be kept by law.
Future projects will receive the required ethics, scientific, data-protection and institutional review, and this is stated.
Re-consent at 16 and limited-capacity constraints (no representative explicit data consent; an HRCDC declaration cannot authorise unknown future research) are addressed.
The document is in English and suitable for the intended Irish population (IE-ICF).
Any other language version for an individual participant is an approved translation and does not replace the English set (IE-HUB).

The person conducting the pre-consent interview and taking consent is the investigator or a registered medical practitioner, dentist or nurse designated by the investigator, consistent with K1 (IE-ICF).

The SIS and ICF match the compensation document (P1); for minors, incapacitated adults and breastfeeding women no incentive beyond expenses or loss of earnings; any token of appreciation flagged for ethics review (IE-PII-CHECKLIST item 9).

Injury and insurance wording matches the insurance or indemnity evidence (O1) and any State indemnity position for the site; no automatic compensation promised where the policy has conditions or exclusions (IE-HV).
Ethics approval statement refers to NREC-CT review (template Part 3).

sections.title: Document inventory, version control and administration (QC 1 and 9)

items.check: Every patient-facing item appears in the Part II document inventory.
Each document has a distinct title, version and date that match its CTIS entry.
Clean and tracked versions are clearly identified where both are supplied.
Site-specific contact details and local procedures are complete.
Superseded versions have not been uploaded by mistake.
The footer is consistent and does not reveal editing comments or internal filenames.
The document can be searched, copied and read with assistive technology; no image-only scans as source documents.
The CTIS submission contains blank, unsigned consent forms, not signed participant copies (IE-ICF).
Hyperlinks, telephone numbers, email addresses, version dates, document names and signature fields are checked (QC 9).

The final participant set is compared with the protocol, IB or product information, recruitment procedure, recruitment materials, site suitability form, compensation form, insurance certificate, Irish data statement and biological-sample form; each discrepancy is recorded with its owner and resolution (QC 9).

No drafting instruction remains in the final version (italic notes, [bracket] notes, 'Drafting note' paragraphs, SAMPLE TEXT labels, ...... gaps, yellow [INSERT/IF/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); fields completed by hand at consent stay blank.
The intended participant can understand the document without specialist knowledge.
Sentences are short and technical terms are defined on first use.
Risk is expressed consistently using words and numbers where useful.
Headings, lists, spacing and page numbering support navigation.
Tables do not hide essential information.
Instructions do not pressure the participant or imply loss of ordinary care for refusal.
Payment wording does not suggest that payment is a benefit of treatment.
The document uses respectful, person-centred language.
If a participant needs another language or communication format, an approved translation or accessible process is planned, without implying that an unpublished Irish-language CTIS guide is available.
